notes: This page only shows the Stephanie mini-doll being put together: lime hair, head, torso and legs. The parts are not in the 41-piece parts list or the catalogue, so I recorded no pieces.
The page has no brick-building step. The French/Spanish choking-hazard warning adds nothing.
Step 1: one lime round brick is stacked on another (b2 on b1).

Step 2: the white 4x4 round plate sits on the top lime brick, with the 6L bar pushed down into its centre hole. I treated the plate as resting on b2 only. Only one lime brick shows under the plate in the picture, but it is the stack from step 1.
The bar's lower end is not shown reaching the lime bricks' axle holes on this page. It may go through them on a later page.
Step 3 has two small sub-assemblies, both added to the white round plate b3.
Left: the white cheese slope goes on the blue milk carton brick, and the pair goes on the plate.
Right: the dark pink flower goes on the reddish brown 1x1 plate, and the pair goes on the plate.
I assumed both the carton brick and the brown plate clutch only b3.
Step 4: the bright pink round plate goes on the goblet, and the goblet stands on the white round plate b3. I assumed the goblet's base sits on b3's studs.

The result picture also shows the blue-and-white printed dish as an umbrella on top of the bar. No step arrow shows it being added, so I recorded it here and joined it to the bar b4. It is the only dish in the parts list. It rests on nothing below, because it only clutches the bar.
The pink plate b10 is one of the 7 bright pink 1x1 round plates.
Step 5: the white round 2x2 tile goes on the third lime round brick, making a stool. The picture shows the stool beside the table, not attached to it, so its first piece rests on nothing.

The remaining-parts list showed one black 1x1 round plate used and no bright pink one, though I recorded the pink plate on the goblet (b10) as bright pink on the last page. The picture shows pink, so I left it.
Step 1: the lime 2x4 plate is the base of a new sub-assembly.
Step 2: the lime 2x2 brick covers one half of the plate and the grey 2x2x2 box covers the other half. Both sit directly on the plate.
The box's door side is open and faces the front right. The door is not attached on this page.
Step 3: a black 1x1 round plate goes on one stud of the grey box (b16). I assumed it is the back-left stud.
Step 4: the clear door is attached to the box's open front with a hinge. The door rests on nothing, because it is held only by the hinge.
The grey box has a clear door added, so the oven is closed.
Sub-step 1: a bright pink 1x1 round plate goes on each stud of the tan 1x2 plate. The picture shows one pink plate already on and the second being added, so I recorded two.
Sub-step 2: the reddish brown 1x2 tile goes across both pink plates.

Step 5: the whole tray assembly is placed on the open clear door b18, which acts as the oven tray. I took the tan plate to clutch the door's studs. The tray is built on the door, which I built earlier in step 5, so the tan plate rests on b18.
The remaining-parts list kept 7 bright pink plates even after the one on the goblet (b10). It seems the earlier plate was counted as black, so the pink count may be off by one.

Step 1: the tan round 2x2 plate goes on the white round grill brick, making the cake. Step 2: two bright pink round plates are stacked on the tan plate, one on the other. Step 3: the cake is set on the pink 3x3 dish. Step 6: the cake and dish go on top of the lime part of the oven (b15).

The dish has no ports in the catalogue, so it only gets rests_on. I put it on b15, with the grill brick's studs going through or over it onto b15. I assumed the cake covers the lime 2x2 brick b15 rather than the grey box with its black plate.

The remaining-parts list still shows 7 bright pink plates even though I recorded some pink ones (b10, b20, b21) earlier. The list seems to have counted those as black. This page adds two more pink plates.
Step 1: the white 2x4 brick is the base of a new sub-assembly, the sink counter.

Step 2: a medium azure 1x2x1 panel and a white 1x2 brick go on the base, one beside the other. Step 3: the second panel and second 1x2 brick go on the free half of the base, so the four pieces cover all eight studs of the base.
I took the exact cell positions from the small pictures, so the left/right and front/back placement is a best guess. The rests_on links are the same either way, because each piece sits only on b28.
Step 4: the grey tap goes on the white 1x2 brick at the right end of the sink (b30). The white and trans-light blue round 1x1 bricks go on the white 1x2 brick at the left end (b32).
Step 5: a bright pink round 1x1 plate goes on each of the two round bricks.
This follows my reading of page 11, where the two 1x2 bricks sit at the ends and the azure panels form the basin between them. The small pictures are not clear on which end each part sits.
Step 4 shows dark plates on the round bricks, but no black plates are left in the parts list. I recorded only the pink plates shown in step 5.
This page shows the finished model: the umbrella table with the mini-doll, the stool, the oven with the cake, and the sink counter. There is no building step, so nothing is added.
One lime 2x2 brick and three bright pink 1x1 round plates are still unplaced. Nothing on this page uses them. They may be spares or appear on a later page.
This page advertises other LEGO Friends sets (3183, 3061, 3065, 3187, 3942, 3936, 3188, 3934, 3315). It has no building step, so nothing is added.
This is the back cover, a LEGOsurvey.com prize draw advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
One lime 2x2 brick (lego-3003) and three bright pink 1x1 round plates were never placed in the booklet. They are probably spare parts. I did not invent placements for them.

Missing lime 2x2 brick: the oven stack is the lime 2x4 plate, then two lime 2x2 bricks, which matches the height of the 2x2x2 box next to it. The second brick b38 sits on b15 (page 7, step 3 or page 8). The cake, dish and its brick b23 then sit on b38, not on b15.

Missing three 1x1 round plates: page 12, step 4 shows dark plates on the white and blue round bricks and one beside the tap. These are the three black plates, which with b17 make the four in the parts list. They are b39 on b34, b40 on b35 and b41 on b30. The pink plates b36 and b37 from step 5 go on top of b39 and b40, so I added those joins.
The bright pink plates now total seven: b10, b20, b21, b25, b26, b36 and b37. This matches the parts list.

Four separate groups are correct for this set. The booklet builds separate toy items for the mini-doll: the umbrella table, the stool, the oven with the cake, and the sink counter. Page 13 shows them standing apart, not touching. I left them unconnected.
The table and the stool are joined only to their own pieces. The stool was built as a separate sub-assembly on page 6, with nothing underneath it.

The four groups are real and I kept them apart. The booklet builds four separate play items: the umbrella table (b1 to b11), the stool (b12, b13), the oven with the cake (b14 to b27, b38) and the sink counter (b28 to b37, b39 to b41). Each has its own numbered steps, and each starts on a fresh base piece.
The booklet's overview picture on page 13 shows the four standing apart with space between them. No step joins one to another, and no piece spans two groups. Any connection would be invented.
The mini-doll on page 2 is not in the parts list and is not recorded.
The previous correction already fixed the real count problems: the missing lime brick b38 and the black plates b39 to b41.
